questions.question: Does AI resume screening reduce bias or actually introduce new bias?
questions.answer_summary: AI screening can perpetuate bias through proxy variables (postcode, school, employment gaps) and historical hiring-data patterns; a cited Brookings-related study found selection-rate gaps as large as 8x between demographic groups on the same tools.

questions.question: Are AI resume-screening tools legally risky for a small business?
questions.answer_summary: Resume-screening AI is classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act and under new state rules such as New Jersey's Division on Civil Rights regulations; Title VII disparate-impact liability still applies even though 2025 federal executive action deprioritized EEOC enforcement.

questions.question: What happened in Mobley v. Workday and why does it matter for AI screening?
questions.answer_summary: Mobley v. Workday is cited as the leading 2025-2026 case shifting AI-hiring-discrimination exposure from federal EEOC action toward private litigation against AI vendors and the employers that use their tools.

questions.question: Do candidates trust AI to evaluate them fairly?
questions.answer_summary: A Greenhouse survey found only 26% of candidates trust AI to evaluate them fairly, and 70% were never clearly told AI would be involved in their screening.

questions.question: What share of candidates walk away from a hiring process because of AI screening?
questions.answer_summary: 38% of candidates have walked away from a hiring process because it included an AI interview, and another 12% say they would; pre-recorded AI-scored video interviews are the single biggest trigger.

questions.question: Should a small company disclose that AI is screening applicants?
questions.answer_summary: 81% of candidates say they'd accept AI screening with guardrails — upfront disclosure, an explanation of what's being measured, and a human-review option — rather than rejecting AI outright.

questions.question: What are affordable AI screening tools built for small teams rather than enterprise TA departments?
questions.answer_summary: Options pitched at small/budget-conscious teams include Willo (Starter plan around $49/month) and Workable, positioned as assist-not-replace tools versus enterprise suites.

questions.question: Can AI screening actually cut cost-per-hire for a small team?
questions.answer_summary: Vendors and adopters claim 20-40% reductions in cost-per-hire when AI handles screening and scheduling, though these are self-reported figures rather than independently audited.

questions.question: Why do LLMs sometimes prefer AI-written resumes over human-written ones?
questions.answer_summary: Research cited found LLMs favored AI-written resumes over human-written resumes by 67-82%, an artifact of writing style rather than candidate quality, which is a specific failure mode small teams using generic chatbots for screening should watch for.

questions.question: What's the difference between AI 'assisting' a human reviewer and AI making the hiring decision?
questions.answer_summary: Guides recommend well-designed AI with human oversight and continuous auditing as the safer middle ground versus letting a model rank-and-reject candidates unsupervised.

questions.question: Are jobseekers organizing against AI-only hiring processes?
questions.answer_summary: Employment lawyers report a 2026 shift from passive frustration to organized pushback — candidates filing state labor-agency complaints and sending demand letters over AI hiring decisions.

questions.question: What are candidates' biggest specific complaints about AI-driven screening?
questions.answer_summary: Top triggers for walking away are pre-recorded video interviews scored by AI with no human present (33%), no disclosure that AI would be used (27%), and AI monitoring during the process (26%).
